Again in 84 (the oversized retention test: a resource failed with the error, then the status read synced) and 85 (the diagnostic invitation's `page.reload`). Investigation 86, time-boxed, found no fix and committed none. What the error means: in WebKit it is `WebLoaderStrategy::internallyFailedLoadTimerFired`, which fails loads when the network process has died (crash or termination), when a load cannot be sent to it, or when Playwright emulates offline (the offline tests print it on every run, harmlessly). In Playwright's WebKit every browser context gets its own network process, which also holds an ephemeral context's localStorage, so its death mid-test fails every load in flight and empties localStorage: that matches 84 exactly (seeded events gone, status synced). `dmesg` holds two network process crashes from 84's failing run (03:44 a general protection fault in `g_type_check_instance_is_fundamentally_a`, 03:47 a segfault in libsoup 3.6.5's `soup_session_unqueue_item`, a freed session feature), so it is a use-after-free in Playwright's WebKit build, not the app; none was logged during 85's run, so 85's cause is unconfirmed. Not reproduced in 86 under load (4 CPU burners, then also the unit and API tests in a loop, load average up to 21): 110 iPhone progress and diagnostic runs, a full three-project run (594 passed), 165 iPhone sign-in, settings, story-sync, learn, progress and diagnostic runs, and 91 network processes watched by an `LD_PRELOAD` probe, with no crash. Ruled out: libsoup feature churn mid-test (the probe saw features added only at start and removed only at context close, which is also the only time a session is disposed, so a crash there cannot fail a test); WebKit killing an unresponsive network process on reload (stalling it 4 and 10 s with SIGSTOP across `page.reload` delayed the reload and kept the process and its localStorage); closing a context or reloading with uploads in flight (150 to 300 rounds each, 704 reloads in one context with aborted, early-answered and reset uploads of up to 300 kB: no failure); and a concurrent `npm run build` in the served worktree, which fails tests differently (404 chunk loads and `{operation: application, category: type}` errors, 3 of 88 runs), though builders must not rebuild the worktree an e2e server is serving. Open: catch a crash in the act, with a preloaded signal handler in the network process that logs a backtrace and the time (to match against the test then running) or a core dump (`ulimit -c unlimited` before Playwright), then report it upstream or move to a Playwright release whose WebKit fixes it. 85's scroll anchoring failure (`code.spec.ts:513`, 635 px at step 36) was not investigated and may be unrelated.
- System design topics after 71: thirty-four, each with a lesson, all reviewed. The initial bundle is 840.5 kB, 19.5 kB
  under its warning.
- Google sign-in on the web has the same race 71 fixed for GitHub: the plugin's Google popup flow also checks once a
  second whether the popup closed and reports a cancel. Recovering it needs the relayed message turned back into a
  Google result; the lasting fix for both is upstream in `@capgo/capacitor-social-login`. Passing our own OAuth `state`
  also reaches the native iOS flow, which honors it; the native builds have not run since.

- Account merge still keeps a destination event on a duplicate ID without checking its payload. A conflicting destination `interview-<session>` event can disagree with the source scorecard moved by that merge. Score completion keeps whichever event is stored first, so merge reconciliation remains separate work.
- Iteration 24 preserves future-dated and oversized events without rewriting timestamps or inventing a repair. It bounds uploads and uses explicit acknowledgments, but full history reads, the local JSON event log and cross-tab coordination remain unbounded or separate work. No automatic retry loop or concurrency certification is implied.
- Only a device's first pull, and the first after signing in or switching accounts, still transfers the whole history
  (about 850 kB for the audit's 4,777 events, 9 s on 3G), so the 20-second pull budget stays; a later pull could take a
  shorter one. The local event log and its acknowledged set are still unbounded: a bounded local checkpoint (replay from a
  saved state plus recent events) is the rest of backlog iteration 11.
- Recent interviews load and return 20 complete transcripts even though the list uses summary fields. Add a lean database/API projection before high-concurrency interview traffic.
- Cold Code workspace navigation still takes 6.50 seconds after the click in the final iteration 23 throttled-phone comparison (was 7.22); the Learn heading takes about nine seconds from page load. Profile dependency and initialization costs before adding more first-entry work. These measurements are heading visibility, not runner startup.
- The offline target in `docs/PLAN.md` is not complete: web route warming supports navigation within an already open tab, but there is no durable offline web startup, and first-use runners can require downloads. Native route assets are bundled, while release Python is downloaded separately. Both scripted and AI interviews require the API. Verify these separately before claiming full offline learning.
- Admin metrics (92) run in SQL in about 6.5 s on 3.3 million events, under their own 30-second limit. The review window
  and the activity bins grow with events; at ten times this size, keep daily rollups (or a per-item last-review table for
  recall) instead. There is still no admin UI for feedback; the API pages it.
- A client query timeout ends the API wait but may leave a write running in Postgres. Progress event IDs make its retry
  idempotent; other write paths need an explicit outcome or idempotency plan before automatic retries are added.
- Refresh tokens (92) are swept a day past expiry, but rotated and revoked ones stay until then: a session refreshing every
  15 minutes keeps up to about 2,900 rows for 30 days. If the table grows too large at 100,000 users, keep only the latest
  rotation plus a reuse marker per family. The sweep runs on warm instances' 10-minute timer; there is no cron. Migration
  `0014` was applied locally on the fixture, not yet rehearsed on a Neon branch.
- Before promoting iteration 18, enable Vercel Standard Deployment Protection and verify a past generated deployment URL
  rejects unauthenticated requests. Old URLs otherwise bypass access-token revocation, and a pre-18 rollback can erase
  without a tombstone.
- Remove migration `0007`'s refresh-token compatibility triggers and function in a later contract release after pre-18
  instances and rollback candidates are inaccessible.
- The signed progress read was 2.2% slower in the clean local comparison (p95 37 to 38 ms); write runs varied under
  autovacuum. Repeat both at audit-sized data and with pooled production-style connections before wider rollout.
- Deleting during an AI reply discards the result, but the provider call can keep running and stream buffered text until
  the learner disconnects or the reply deadline (90 s, 81) cancels it. Add upstream cancellation on deletion.
- Scoring is a non-streaming call, so one cut off by its deadline (81) reports no usage and keeps its whole hold. Streaming
  the scorer (and not retrying it once connected) would let it settle at the input it reported plus the output cap, as a
  cut-off reply does.
- Visualizer at 320 px: some verdicts (about 40 of 144 checkpoints) are taller than the space above the playback controls,
  so the reveal keeps the controls on screen and the verdict's end sits under them until the learner scrolls. The first
  question can also open under the tab bar at 320 px.
- Binary Search with a long custom input such as -100 scrolls sideways inside the array on phones (by design since
  iteration 11, cells keep one width for the whole trace); a wrapped or compact layout would avoid the scroll.
- Scrolled arrays cannot be reached by keyboard in Safari, which skips scrollable regions in the tab order.
- Desktop at 1280x720: the sticky stage can jump when a checkpoint makes it taller than the side column.
- Resizing a desktop visualizer across the 960 px breakpoint and back, with the drawing's top within a few px of the
  toolbar: the page can come back 88 to 156 px off (dijkstra at 1366x660, 4 of 48 placements), or the next step can shift
  the drawing 45 to 111 px (grid-bfs, 2 of 48). Narrowing jumps about 800 px in Chrome before and after iteration 11.
  `HoldHeightDirective` switches native anchoring off while the drawing's top is above the view, so the widening is not
  anchored.
- `HoldHeightDirective` picks its rule by whether the drawing's top is on screen, not the controls; within 0 to 5 px of the
  toolbar a step's own compensation can cross that line, and the Code panel then moves (tree-traversal on Pixel 7).
- With predict mode on, a keyboard checkpoint round trip leaves the Code panel 8 px off on phones (union-find 72 px).
- At 400% zoom, `reveal()` never scrolls up, so a focused narration can end above the view (2 of 144 checkpoints). After a
  keyboard Continue at 200% and above, the focused narration wins over keeping Step forward on screen.
- Two-column page end: the sticky stage grows upward, so Step forward can move as the drawing grows (trie at 1366x660, up
  to 215 px).
- The Code panel's lit-line scroll uses `offsetTop` against `ion-content`, not the panel; it works only while panels overflow
  by 75 px or less.
- Arrow keys on the focused, scrollable Array region both step the player and scroll the region.
- The checkpoint's "Your call" icon shifts the panel 5 px when it loads.
- The interview title is truncated at 320 px.
- The shared-code snapshot label uses "1 lines" for a single line; pluralize it.
- At 320 px, in both themes, content scrolled under the toolbar shows faintly through it behind the title (the Predict mode
  switch reads through on an answered Subsets checkpoint); the same on `main`.
- The pattern page's first tap is 44 to 133 ms slower than before iteration 10, because the full pattern content now loads
  on tap (about 3 kB brotli). Faster from page load overall.
- Trace: a generator resumed by a different call becomes a new call in the call stack, and a paused generator's node reads
  "returned" while it is off the stack.
- Native: the splash screen stays dark in the light theme; status bar icons on a light launch need a check on a device.
- Dependabot's `@sentry/angular` update fails CI.
- The generic screenshot audit now isolates each context with a unique learner ID, resolving shared server history between states. The supplemental offline harness still needs an explicit transition-completion condition; its 500 ms wait is shorter than Ionic's 540 ms default.
- The tree view's side spot (a badge above and beside its node) is covered by a unit test and the code-trace measure, but
  no audit state shows it; a traced skewed tree (such as `[1,2,null,3]`) in `tools/verify` would.
- Tree badges with long pointer names still cross a link where neighbouring badges crowd a lopsided tree: 87 of 14,716 in
  the long-name code traces (`current_node` and `previous_node` in random trees of 7 to 46 nodes); the problem examples
  draw 0. A badge naming several pointers wraps past 13 characters even where one line would fit (`treeRootNode, node`
  above a root). The side room comes from laying out every frame once per trace: 0.2 to 0.3 ms for the problem examples,
  20 to 37 ms for a 63-node tree over 448 frames. Layout per frame in real traces stays within about 10% of `main`;
  synthetic trees with every node badged `current_node, previous_node` are 4.7 to 5.4x slower (255 nodes: 68 ms), from the
  second round of placement.
- A cloud run of this loop cannot finish a release: its container could not reach the production URL (egress proxy), its
  Node is 22.22.2 (the Angular CLI needs 24, per `.nvmrc`) and its Chromium is 141 (pinned 153). Iteration 12 was
  finished and verified from a local session.
- CI minutes: Dependabot rebases re-run full CI and the native builds (macOS included) on every new sha, about 480 of 2,230
  Linux-equivalent minutes from 2026-09-20 to 09-26. `rebase-strategy: disabled` in `.github/dependabot.yml` (rebase with
  `@dependabot rebase` before merging) would stop that; it changes how the owner handles Dependabot, so it is their call.
- CI minutes: each of the four end-to-end shards builds the app and bills 3 minutes (12 of CI's 19). Two shards would bill
  about 8 for about 70 s more wall time; try it on a branch.
- A deploy by hand does not require a passing CI run of the commit, so `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`'s "nothing reaches production
  without CI" holds only for `main`. A first step in `deploy.yml` that fails without one would close that.
- CI: the four end-to-end shards are uneven (118, 136, 175 and 185 s after iteration 11; CI 191 s wall, was 159 to 169 s).
  Playwright 1.63 splits by test count, not duration. Record per-test durations (`--reporter=json`, 336 s over 222 tests
  locally) and feed each shard a balanced `--test-list`.
- A worktree whose `node_modules` is a symlink to the main checkout builds the app and API against the main checkout's
  `libs/engine/dist` (`@grasp/engine` resolves through that checkout's workspace link), so new engine content is missing
  from the build and the browser tests. Iteration 15 gave its worktree a `node_modules` of links with its own `@grasp` ones.
- On a failed test of a problem compared in any order (Two Sum, Top K Frequent, Subsets), Expected and Output list their
  items in different orders, so a missing Subsets subset means scanning two differently ordered lists. Sorting both the
  same way for display would line the mismatch up.
- `graphs.ts` still holds the two tree problems, which can move to `problems/trees.ts` with the next tree problem.
- Parallel Courses keeps the longest prerequisite path at 37 so memoized recursive DFS works in browser JavaScript and
  Python; WebKit's Python can crash near 40 levels with `@cache` plus a generator. Its performance case times out naive
  DFS and per-course relation scans, but prepared semester rescans and Bellman-Ford-style relaxation rounds pass within
  2 s. Making those variants time out would need a graph too large for the app's memory budget.
- The Python prelude now allows 10,000 recursive frames, and its crash message explains `functools` cache stack limits.
  Coin Change still needs a dict memo or bottom-up code in Pyodide when cached recursion gets deep. House Robber's
  100,000-house performance case is too deep for a top-down recursive solution in browser JavaScript or Python; set a
  consistent policy for large DP problems if these alternatives should pass.
- Linked lists (78): code traces show each list variable as the values it leads to (`2 → 1`), not a drawing with
  pointer badges as trees get; a drawn list, like the Reverse a Linked List visualizer's, would show which node each
  pointer is on. The Python harness unlinks every predefined `ListNode` made during a call and the list returned, so
  browser Python never frees a long chain of them recursively; a long chain of a learner's own node class that is never
  returned can still crash browser Python, which then recovers as for any crash. The performance cases (2·10^5 nodes)
  are too deep for a recursive solution in either browser language, as the statements say.
- The WebKit scroll jump (61, 63, 69) is fixed in 70 by excluding the held drawing from scroll anchoring. If Step forward
  jumps again on iPhone, keep `test-results` and check the painted screencast frames before anything else.
- iPhone (WebKit) tests fail now and then only under the full suite and pass alone: the scroll jump above, `page.goto`
  internal errors (63), and the feedback dialog's Ctrl/⌘ + Enter check (code.spec.ts:148, 65). Worth one reliability
  iteration: fewer WebKit workers, or retries that record a trace so the failures can be read.
- Code traces can place scalar variables named `right`, `end` or `i` over unrelated arrays as index markers. Track actual
  index use before drawing these markers, including learner code.
- Small refactors: move `DEVICE_PLATFORM` into `platform.ts`; confirm the notifications plugin proxy is cleaned up on destroy.

- Public reads after 95: after the next release, check that a repeated anonymous `GET /api/auth/config` on production returns `x-vercel-cache: HIT` (without an `Authorization` header). `/config.json` and deep-link page loads still invoke the function on every app start with `no-cache`; caching them at the CDN is backlog item 14. Every other route still writes one counter (two for anonymous learners) per request, and at 100,000 simultaneous users those writes, not client connections, bound Neon: an in-memory pre-check or batched counters would cut them, and a Vercel WAF rate rule on `/api/*` would cover volumetric abuse of the uncounted public reads. The seeded `review-items/:id/question?seed=` is deterministic and could be a public read too; nothing calls it today. Uncounted cache misses: a random query string or `Origin` value makes every request a CDN miss on a public read, which then costs function CPU and egress (no database work); mitigate with a Vercel firewall rule, or by answering 400 to any query string on the public reads. The pool model is local and arithmetic: measure warm-instance counts, pooler waits and 503s on a Neon branch with production-style load before a wider release.

- Design Lab after 96: cache and CDN hit rates are still node settings the learner controls (up to 99%), so a CDN at 99%
  eats every read in any mission, even private mail or ledger balances; read-heavy missions (feature flags, proximity)
  need the cacheable share in the workload, as the object share now is. The existing six missions name no object share,
  so an object store still takes 30% of their app traffic (or the share an old board saved on it, since mission boards
  keep the old rule and missions hide the Files slider) and The Write Wall still passes for $5,650 with workers writing
  only to a store; naming `objectShare: 0` on them closes it but changes saved boards that use a store. The email, video
  and crawler builds name no share and keep the instance-count split (the CDN and transcoders send a third of their
  traffic to Segments); naming one moves every file to the store and changes their numbers. Code Deployment's build sends
  30% of control-plane requests to the artifact store although its text says bytes reach hosts through caches and peers.
  The share applies to reads and writes alike, so a mission cannot say "downloads are files, uploads are not".

## Redesign

On 2026-10-02 the owner approved `docs/REDESIGN.md` as proposed. It rebuilds the navigation around the rounds of an
interview loop (Today, Coding, Design, Behavioral and Mock, with a left rail on desktop) and moves every interactive
picture onto one shared kit, the Workbench language. It ships as 49 iterations, R0 to R48, in the order and with the
dependencies of its section 5.1, each through the gates of its section 5.0. Until R16 has landed (navigation, Today and
the hubs), it takes priority over the content ideas below; after that, content items may interleave with the remaining
redesign iterations.

R0 (97) built the gates the later iterations run, as `tools/verify/README.md` describes. Its decisions, so later runs
need not rediscover them:

- **First paint.** Angular's `initial` budget (850 kB warning, 855 kB error) is 5.0's backstop; the script does not
  measure the initial total again. The gate is the line `npm run build` prints in the app's `postbuild`
  (`apps/app/scripts/first-paint-bytes.mjs`, on the `stats.json` every production build writes), not
  `first-paint-bytes.test.mjs` as 5.0 says: that file tests the logic on fixtures (REDESIGN.md 5.0 now has a note). It
  fails 2 kB below the baseline as well as above, so an iteration that shrinks first paint (R9) commits the lower
  baseline. Its total includes the global stylesheet, a deliberate superset of 5.0's closure, so R6 and R7's
  `styles.scss` growth is measured. The viz allowlist (`mastery-ring`, `code-text`) fails once a module leaves first
  paint, so R7 and R9 remove their entries.
- **Style ratchet.** It counts more than 3.2 lists (literal colors, SVG attributes, bindings, TypeScript strings, mixin
  arguments, laundered sizes); `tools/verify/README.md` lists every rule. The decisions: only `_theme.scss` and the root
  rules of `styles.scss` define tokens, so a theme name set anywhere else (a component, or a component rule in
  `styles.scss`) counts where it is set; it enforces from R0; and `@media` at the sanctioned 560, 1024 and 1280px (and
  559.98, 1023.98, 1279.98) never counts, so R1, R2 and R10 need no hand raise for those breakpoints, and R6's "report to
  enforce" is the tokens and mixins that let counts fall.
- **Motion test mode.** The audit and Playwright set only `data-motion="off"`, on the context, before any app script;
  `?motion=off` is R3's to add with its boot code, which strips it (26 `toHaveURL(/…$/)` assertions would otherwise
  break). Nothing reads either until R3.
- **Tablet.** The `tablet` project runs only with `E2E_TABLET=1` (5.0's subset:
  `E2E_TABLET=1 npm run e2e -- --project=tablet`), so `npm run e2e`, CI and production smoke stay on three devices. A
  tagged test that fails on the tablet for an app reason keeps its tag with
  `test.fixme(testInfo.project.name === 'tablet', '<reason>')` and a follow-up here.
- **Audit.** A state is clean only with 0 axe violations of any impact (5.0), no page error and no overflow; every
  violation is recorded with its impact. pixdiff fails when a state clean in the stored set is not clean in the new
  capture; known failures are listed in R0's Shipped entry.
- **Native builds.** `native.yml` ignores the two gate scripts and their baselines, so an iteration that only moves a
  baseline runs no macOS build.
- **Stored set.** `/var/tmp/grasp-shots/a177434/` (desktop, w1024, pixel7, w320, both themes); `tools/verify/README.md`
  says how to check it is current and how each iteration refreshes it. Because every axe impact now fails a state, the
  production audit in CLAUDE.md exits 1 only on a real failure (R1 fixed `behavioral-story` in the capture and the
  320px forecast spill).
- **No app changes in R0.** A new state that found an app problem (the 320px spill) is recorded, not fixed, so the
  build stayed identical to the base and the baselines describe `main`.

  fall.
- R5 or R10: decide whether CI runs the tablet subset (one WebKit shard, about 8 to 12 Linux runner-minutes a run).

## Content ideas

The owner's direction (2026-09-28): as much learning and practice content as possible across algorithms, system design and
behavioral interviews, as interactive as possible with many examples, for landing jobs at the largest companies, serving
100,000 simultaneous users. On 2026-09-30 the owner asked to fill the content gaps with great quality content first. On
2026-10-02 the owner approved this order, mixing content with the scale work a wide release needs. Every piece keeps the
bar so far: numbers come from a model the widget runs, an independent agent reviews facts, arithmetic and answer
choices, and each gets review items.

Done: the behavioral AI interviewer (74, 76), the missing patterns (78 to 80), the dated study plan (83), the full mock
loop (84), and the payment ledger, feature flag, proximity, email and code deployment cases (87, 88, 91, 93, 94).

Next, in order:

1. Design Lab missions with three spaced revisits each: done in 96. The object store's share moved into the workload,
   and Attachments Everywhere, Month-End Ledger and Reconnect Storm shipped; missions for the read-heavy builds (feature
   flags, proximity) wait for the cacheable share in the workload (see the follow-ups).
2. Object-oriented design rounds, the biggest gap for Amazon, Microsoft and Uber style loops: an engine and runner for
   class design problems (parking lot, elevator, LRU and LFU caches, iterators), then a first problem set. About two
   iterations.
3. Behavioral depth: for each of the 13 competencies, a weak, a better and a strong answer with the flaw named, and the
   AI interviewer's live eval run on GPT-6 Luna. About two iterations.
4. Scale work before a wide release (from the production readiness backlog and the follow-ups): cheaper rate limiting
   so non-cached routes stop writing one or two Postgres counters per request, a defined workload, and a load test on a
   Neon branch for 100,000 simultaneous users, then fixing what it finds. About three or four iterations.
5. Missing coding patterns, one per iteration: stack parsing (calculators, brackets), matrix and simulation, string
   algorithms (KMP, rolling hash), segment and Fenwick trees, more graphs (bipartite, Bellman-Ford). Also a Find the
   Shortest Superstring problem and a `dp[mask][last]` visualizer for bitmask DP.
6. Classic system design cases still missing: a distributed key-value store (Dynamo style), object storage (S3 style)
   and a unique ID generator.
7. More problems per pattern (toward 10 to 12) and more drill cards and clozes for the thinnest patterns (36 clozes
   across 23 patterns today); consider a secondary greedy tag for Non-overlapping Intervals.
8. The remaining production readiness items (14, 15, and the partial 4, 6, 8, 11), native crash reporting and the
   Android emulator smoke test, and the Playwright WebKit crash, interleaved every two or three content iterations.

## Rules for picking

- Prefer what a learner notices: correctness bugs, then accessibility and layout problems, then speed, then new content,
  then internal cleanups.
- Fix rounds run only the affected browser specs on desktop after typecheck, unit tests and the build; the full suite
  (verify and every browser project) runs once, on the head that fast-forwards. When that head's tree is the one a builder
  already ran `npm run verify` on, the build and the browser suite are enough, since CI runs verify on the push.
- One cohesive improvement per run. Measure before and after; never ship a change that makes something else slower or
  worse without saying so here.
